header:
Date: 2025-10-22
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 50m
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Jamal Lee (Redwood SE), Sofia Chen (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (ScaleLayer Head of ML), Tom Gallagher (Infra), Lena Ortiz (SRE)
Recording: Fireflies auto transcript (medium quality)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot throughput numbers and tuning steps. Team validated continuous batching improvements, identified queueing hot spots during burst windows, agreed to run targeted concurrent benchmarks and share logs. Action items include updated pricing spreadsheet and a follow-up deep dive on queue policy and autoscaler settings.
topics: KV cache warmup and hit rates
transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got a packed agenda for the 50 minute sync, quick round robin?
[00:10] Priya: Hi, Priya here, head of ML at ScaleLayer, Tom and Lena are with me.
[00:15] Tom: Hey all.
[00:18] Lena: hi.
[00:22] Jamal: Jamal from Redwood SE, I'll lead the perf section.
[00:25] Sofia: Sofia from CSM, scope/next steps.
[00:30] Ava: Great, first — quick recap of last week's baseline: we saw 320 rps with default batching and unstable p95. We pushed the continuous batching patch and saw a preliminary bump. Jamal, can you walk numbers?
[01:00] Jamal: Sure. So with continuous batching + kv cache enabled (note: kv cash in some logs), we saw effective throughput hit about 1.1k to 1.3k reqs per second on the 2x baseline rig. p50 was 40ms, p95 around 260ms, p99 occasionally spike to 1.8s during cold starts. The big win was tokens/sec; we moved from ~45k tokens/s to roughly 160k tokens/s for the same cost bucket.
[01:40] Priya: That sounds promising. That p99 spike — is that due to cold KV cache warms or queue buildup?
[01:48] Jamal: It's both. We saw two modes: coldshot spikes when model workers are spun up, and queueing spikes when there's a momentary burst of small requests that don't batch well by size. Continuous batching helps but we still have jitter from the prefetch window.
[02:10] Tom: On our side we instrumented the request traces — a lot of the tail looks like context fetches from our DB plus a 10–15ms network hop. Could be adding to variance.
[02:24] Lena: Also noted our ingress spikes at 80 qps for short windows, then flattens. We'd like stable p95 under 350ms.
[02:35] Ava: Ok, objective set — keep p95 < 350ms during your typical burst profile. Jamal, what tuning knobs did we test?
[02:45] Jamal: We tried three variables: target concurrency per worker (1, 2, 4), continuous batching window (2–8ms), and queueing policy (FIFO vs priority). Concurrency=2 with batching window ~4ms hit the sweet spot for throughput vs tail. Concurrency=4 increased throughput but p95 regressed unless we increased batch size caps.
[03:15] Priya: Do we have concrete numbers for concurrency=2 vs 4?
[03:20] Jamal: Yes — concurrency=2: throughput ~1.2k rps, p95 ~260ms. Concurrency=4: throughput ~1.8k rps but p95 went up to ~480ms unless we allowed larger batches which added latency for small requests.
[03:45] Priya: So tradeoff is clear — higher throughput but worse latency unless we tune batch formation heuristics.
[03:50] Ava: For the POC, what's our recommended target?
[03:54] Jamal: For ScaleLayer's workload (mix of short interactive and long completions), start with concurrency target 2, batching window 4ms, max batch tokens 4096, and enable KV cache with warmup prefetch. See notes I uploaded.
[04:10] Tom: On the KV cache warmup — how do you recommend we pre-warm? We can't afford full model warmups every restart.
[04:20] Jamal: Use early prefixes that mirror common requests and run a small parallel prewarm job on the dedicated pool. Also set cache eviction thresholds to avoid thrash. We saw warm hit rate go from 12% to 74% after targeted prewarm.
[04:40] Priya: That's a big delta. Is prewarm included in the POC cost?
[04:44] Ava: We'll include a conservative estimate in the updated pricing sheet.
[04:48] Lena: Back to queueing — when bursts happen, do we have mechanisms to prioritize critical requests? For example, interactive chat over async batch jobs.
[04:58] Jamal: Yes, we can tag priority routes and give them smaller batching windows or a dedicated fast lane. The queueing policy can be priority-first for those tagged routes. But that reduces effective achievable throughput on the cheap tier.
[05:18] Priya: Could we do hybrid — priority for small interactive, and aggressive batching for long-running completions?
[05:24] Jamal: Exactly, that's common. We tested a two-queue system: interactive queue with max batch size 8 and window 2ms, and bulk queue with window 8ms and batch token cap 4096. That kept interactive p95 under 200ms while bulk throughput remained high.
[05:46] Tom: Interesting. Any differences across GPU types? We're testing on A100 and an older T4 cluster.
[05:54] Jamal: A100s obviously give better per-gpu throughput and lower kernel latency. On T4 we had to lower concurrency and rely more on quantization to hit the same latency targets. We also saw kernel selection mismatches in the older drivers — that caused some microstutters.
[06:12] Priya: For production we are leaning toward mixed; can Redwood route based on region and GPU profile?
[06:18] Ava: Yes, smart routing can route by policy — latency or cost — and fallback to compatible model variant. We'll show an example policy in the follow-up doc.
[06:28] Priya: Great. On autoscale — current POC policy is reactive; we want to avoid cascading spin-ups that create p99 spikes. Any suggestions?
[06:36] Jamal: We recommend proactive warmup windows and scale-up thresholds on request rate with a short cool-down. Also keep a small buffer of spare workers (burst pool) that can take short bursts without spinup. That reduced cold-start tail by ~60% in our internal tests.
[07:00] Lena: Is the burst pool an extra cost? How is it priced?
[07:06] Ava: It depends — in Dedicated mode it's part of capacity planning; in Hosted we can enable burst and charge for minutes used beyond commit. We'll add the example pricing in the sheet.
[07:16] Priya: Ok. Jamal, you mentioned prefetch and KV cache hit improvements — can you share the profiler traces?
[07:22] Jamal: Yes I've uploaded a tar with profiler logs to the shared folder — note some filenames have 'kv-cash' spelled incorrectly in the automated pipeline.
[07:32] Tom: (laughs) we've seen the 'cash' issue. We'll look.
[07:36] Jamal: Also important: request size distribution matters — small short requests batch differently and cause fragmentation. We recommend classifying routes and setting per-route batching policies.
[07:48] Priya: We'll produce a route map by tomorrow.
[07:52] Ava: Perfect. Quick check — did we run the concurrency=2 benchmark with 64 token average lengths?
[07:58] Jamal: Yes — numbers I quoted earlier are for 64 token avg. For 256 token average, throughput drops roughly 35% but latency smooths out because batching shapes better.
[08:12] Priya: So longer context favors batching and gives better utilization. Good to know.
[08:18] Tom: Any specific logging we should enable to diagnose tail spikes?
[08:22] Jamal: Trace sampling on p95/p99 traces, and include event markers for cache misses, model load, queue wait time. That will let us separate network/DB vs runtime stalls.
[08:34] Priya: We'll enable the sampling and share traces.
[08:38] Ava: Let's get into the short benchmark run we did yesterday — Jamal, can you narrate the seq of tests and results?
[08:44] Jamal: Sure. Test A: baseline on default batching, concurrency=1 → 320 rps. Test B: continuous batching patch, concurrency=2, kv cache prewarm → 1.2k rps. Test C: concurrency=4, larger batch cap → 1.8k rps but p95 high. Test D: two-queue hybrid with priority small window → interactive p95 180ms, bulk throughput ~1.5k rps. We recorded GPU util and kernel stalls — attached in logs.
[09:20] Lena: What's the GPU util numbers?
[09:23] Jamal: A100 nodes hit ~78–92% util depending on batch formation; T4 were 60–72% with more variability.
[09:30] Priya: Any memory pressure?
[09:33] Jamal: With concurrency=4 we saw higher memory working set and occasional eviction-induced stalls; quantization helped but not eliminate.
[09:42] Tom: Did you try micro-batching within a worker or cross-worker aggregation?
[09:47] Jamal: We do continuous batching across requests hitting the same worker. Cross-worker aggregation isn't trivial without increasing routing latency. We tested a small coordinator but it introduced extra network hop.
[09:58] Priya: Understood. On error-handling — when queue overflow happens, what's recommended? Drop, retry, or reroute?
[10:04] Jamal: For interactive route we prefer reroute to a degraded model variant or a fallback with deterministic shorter responses; for non-critical batch jobs we queue with backpressure and retries. Avoid blind drops.
[10:16] Ava: Good. Any legal/security blockers?
[10:19] Priya: We're still waiting on SAML SSO integration details and audit log retention numbers.
[10:24] Sofia: I'll attach the SOC2 docs and SSO integration guide in the follow-up.
[10:29] Priya: Thanks. Back to perf — can we try a 2x concurrency run with burst pool enabled and priority queueing?
[10:36] Jamal: Yes — I'll schedule that overnight and upload results.
[10:40] Tom: When you run overnight, please include both A100 and T4 traces so we can compare.
[10:45] Jamal: Will do.
[10:47] Priya: For acceptance criteria: we'd like sustained 1k rps with p95 <350ms during our nominal bursts and cost <$0.08 per 1k tokens (example). Can Redwood help estimate that?
[10:58] Ava: We'll model cost in the spreadsheet; I'll include projected per-token cost at your target config and the Dedicated commit options.
[11:08] Priya: Thanks. Two quick misc questions — are there any known regressions with the newest runtime? We had a report of tokenization mismatch last week.
[11:15] Jamal: We fixed a tokenizer edge case in the last patch; that shouldn't affect runtime perf. There is a minor change in kernel scheduling that can reduce latency variance but may reduce throughput slightly on older GPUs. We'll document the tradeoff.
[11:34] Tom: Noted.
[11:36] Ava: Ok recapping next steps: Ava to send pricing spreadsheet and example autoscale/burst config; Jamal to run 2x concurrency+burstpool+priority queueing benchmarks across A100/T4 and upload logs; Priya to share route map and traffic profile; schedule follow-up deep dive w SREs. Any other asks?
[11:58] Priya: Please also include a short note on how quantization impacted T4 results.
[12:04] Jamal: Yep will add that section.
[12:08] Lena: And can we get the profiler markers for cache miss vs model load?
[12:12] Jamal: I'll make sure they're present in the upload.
[12:16] Ava: Great. We'll aim to reconvene after logs are in — likely 2025-10-29 for the deep dive. Thanks everyone.
[12:24] Priya: Thanks all.
[12:27] Tom: bye.
[12:28] Lena: bye.
[12:30] Ava: bye.

Notes: transcript contains typical Fireflies mis-transcriptions ("kv cash", occasional missing punctuation). References to shared artifacts: link to /shared/ScaleLayer/poc-logs.tar.gz (uploaded), /shared/ScaleLayer/poc-pricing-v2.xlsx (to be uploaded by Ava).
